description: Change of use from Use Class C3 (dwelling house) to a Class Sui Generis (HMO - house in multiple occupation) involving part single, part 2-storey side/rear extension and rear dormer, with associated amenity, cycle and refuse storage.
decision_conditions: The proposed large sui generis HMO, accommodating up to 8 occupants, would significantly intensify activity compared to a single-family dwelling. The associated comings and goings of occupants and their visitors and the associated infrastructure required (car parking, commercial bins, cycle parking) for an HMO of the scale would  harm the established residential character of the area and would introduce a commercial operation in an area dominated by single family dwellinghouses. The proposal is therefore contrary to Policies CP5 and CP30 of the Enfield Core Strategy (2010), Policies DMD5, DMD8 and DMD68 of the Enfield Development Management Document (2014), and Policies D3 and D14 of the London Plan (2021).

The development, by virtue of its scale and intensity of occupation, would result in unacceptable levels of noise and general disturbance, harming the amenities of neighbouring residential occupiers. The proposal is therefore contrary to Policy DMD 68, DMD 8 and DMD 5 of the Enfield Development Management Document (2014), and D14 of the London Plan (2021), and Section 12 of the National Planning Policy Framework (2024).

The proposed development, by reason of the siting, scale and depth of the first-floor rear extension, would result in an unacceptable loss of light and outlook for the neighbouring occupiers at No. 41 Bridgenhall Road. In particular, the extension would infringe the 30-degree splay line when assessed from the nearest habitable room window, resulting in an overbearing form of development and a heightened sense of enclosure which would be detrimental to the residential amenities of the adjoining occupier. The proposal is therefore contrary to Policies DMD11 and DMD8 of the Development Management Document (2014)

The proposed development fails to satisfactorily demonstrate the amount of on-site car parking that could be safely and independently accommodated and accessed on the site, having regard to the constraints of the existing dropped kerb and boundary treatment. As a result, the development is likely to lead to overspill parking onto the surrounding highway network, to the detriment of public parking availability for existing residents and road users, potentially impacting highway safety. The proposal is therefore contrary to Policies DMD8 and DMD47 of the Development Management Document and Policy T6 of the London Plan (2021).

The proposed development fails to provide safe, secure and accessible cycle parking. Whilst cycle storage has been indicated within the rear garden, access is via a side passage of insufficient width to allow practical and convenient use. It is unclear whether cycle parking could be successfully provided to the front of the site given the competing demands for use of this space (car parking and refused storage) and as such, the proposed cycle parking as currently proposed, and in the absence of a clear alternative, is not considered usable in practice and fails to meet required standards. The proposal is therefore contrary to Policies DMD8 and DMD47 of the Development Management Document and Policy T5 of the London Plan (2021), which require development to provide accessible and functional cycle parking provision.
